answer.en: In Client/Server architecture, one dedicated computer (the server) provides resources or services to other computers (clients), while in Peer to Peer architecture, all computers have equal status and can act as both client and server.
answer.ne: In Client/Server architecture, one dedicated computer (the server) provides resources or services to other computers (clients), while in Peer to Peer architecture, all computers have equal status and can act as both client and server.

solution.en: Two differences: (1) Client/Server has a centralized, dedicated server managing resources, whereas Peer to Peer has no central server - every computer shares its own resources directly. (2) Client/Server is generally more secure and easier to manage centrally, while Peer to Peer is simpler and cheaper to set up but harder to secure and manage as the network grows.

title.ne: Group B - Q5: Dry run the given program

solution.en: A starts at 5 and is passed to SUB Series(A). The loop runs K = 1 to 5. In each pass, the current value of A is printed first (with a trailing semicolon, so all values print on the same line), and then A is doubled (A = A*2) before the next iteration. So: K=1 prints 5, A becomes 10; K=2 prints 10, A becomes 20; K=3 prints 20, A becomes 40; K=4 prints 40, A becomes 80; K=5 prints 80, A becomes 160 (this final 160 is never printed).
solution.ne: A starts at 5 and is passed to SUB Series(A). The loop runs K = 1 to 5. In each pass, the current value of A is printed first (with a trailing semicolon, so all values print on the same line), and then A is doubled (A = A*2) before the next iteration. So: K=1 prints 5, A becomes 10; K=2 prints 10, A becomes 20; K=3 prints 20, A becomes 40; K=4 prints 40, A becomes 80; K=5 prints 80, A becomes 160 (this final 160 is never printed).

items.code:
DECLARE SUB Series (A)
CLS
A = 5
CALL Series (A)
END

SUB Series (A)
 FOR K = 1 TO 5
    PRINT A;
    A = A*2
 NEXT K
END SUB

title.en: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program
title.ne: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

answer.en: The program has four bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement, an invalid string-function call, and CLOSE using a filename instead of a file number.
answer.ne: The program has four bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement, an invalid string-function call, and CLOSE using a filename instead of a file number.

solution.en: (1) 'OPEN "See.dat" for OUTPUT AS #2' would erase the existing file; since the comment says a record should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #2'. (2) 'INPUT #2, N$, A$, C' reads from the file instead of writing to it; to add a record it must be 'PRINT #2, N$, A$, C'. (3) 'UCASE (Y$)' is invalid QBASIC syntax for a string function - the correct form is 'UCASE$(Y$)' with the dollar sign. (4) 'CLOSE "See.dat"' is invalid, since CLOSE takes a file number, not a filename; it must be 'CLOSE #2' to match the file number used when opening.
solution.ne: (1) 'OPEN "See.dat" for OUTPUT AS #2' would erase the existing file; since the comment says a record should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #2'. (2) 'INPUT #2, N$, A$, C' reads from the file instead of writing to it; to add a record it must be 'PRINT #2, N$, A$, C'. (3) 'UCASE (Y$)' is invalid QBASIC syntax for a string function - the correct form is 'UCASE$(Y$)' with the dollar sign. (4) 'CLOSE "See.dat"' is invalid, since CLOSE takes a file number, not a filename; it must be 'CLOSE #2' to match the file number used when opening.

items.code:
REM to add record in an existing file
CLS
OPEN "See.dat" FOR APPEND AS #2
BB:
  INPUT "Enter the Name"; N$
  INPUT "Enter the Address"; A$
  INPUT "Enter the Class"; C
  PRINT #2, N$, A$, C
  INPUT "More record"; Y$
  IF UCASE$(Y$) = "Y" THEN GOTO BB
CLOSE #2
END

DECLARE FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
DIM SHARED A$, B$, C$
CLS
READ A$, B$, C$
DATA "NEPAL", "BANGLADESH", "BHUTAN"
PRINT LongestName$ (Z$)
END

FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
  L$=A$
  IF LEN(B$) > LEN(L$) THEN
     L$ = B$
  ELSEIF LEN (C$)>LEN(L$) THEN
     L$=C$
  END IF
  LongestName$=L$
END FUNCTION

solution.en: The main module takes three numbers A, B, and C as input. It calls the Sub procedure Total(A, B, C) using CALL, which computes and prints A+B+C directly since a sub does not return a value to the caller. items.code:
DECLARE SUB Total (A, B, C)
DECLARE FUNCTION Average (A, B, C)

CLS
INPUT "Enter first number: ", A
INPUT "Enter second number: ", B
INPUT "Enter third number: ", C

CALL Total(A, B, C)
PRINT "Average = "; Average(A, B, C)

END

SUB Total (A, B, C)
    Sum = A + B + C
    PRINT "Sum = "; Sum
END SUB

FUNCTION Average (A, B, C)
    Average = (A + B + C) / 3
END FUNCTION

answer.en: A QBASIC program that creates "STUDENT.TXT" and stores Roll No, Name, Class, Date of Birth, and Address for as many students as the user wants, as shown in the code field.
answer.ne: A QBASIC program that creates "STUDENT.TXT" and stores Roll No, Name, Class, Date of Birth, and Address for as many students as the user wants, as shown in the code field.

solution.en: The file "STUDENT.TXT" is opened FOR OUTPUT, which creates it if it does not already exist. A DO...LOOP WHILE loop repeatedly asks the user for a student's Roll No, Name, Class, Date of Birth, and Address, and writes each record to the file using WRITE #1. After each record, the user is asked whether to add more data; the loop continues as long as the answer is "Y", letting the user input as many records as needed. Finally the file is closed.

A DO...LOOP WHILE loop repeatedly asks the user for a student's Roll No, Name, Class, Date of Birth, and Address, and writes each record to the file using WRITE #1. After each record, the user is asked whether to add more data; the loop continues as long as the answer is "Y", letting the user input as many records as needed. Finally the file is closed.

items.code:
OPEN "STUDENT.TXT" FOR OUTPUT AS #1
CLS
DO
    INPUT "Enter Roll No: ", RollNo
    INPUT "Enter Name: ", Name$
    INPUT "Enter Class: ", Class$
    INPUT "Enter Date of Birth: ", DOB$
    INPUT "Enter Address: ", Address$
    WRITE #1, RollNo, Name$, Class$, DOB$, Address$
    INPUT "Add more data (Y/N): ", Ans$
LOOP WHILE UCASE$(Ans$) = "Y"
CLOSE #1
END
